_comment: RDPeek's known-bad graphics-driver advisory list. Community-maintained — open a PR to add or correct entries. RDPeek fetches the raw copy of this file from GitHub at runtime (falling back to the copy embedded in the build) and warns when a client- or server-side display adapter matches. MATCHING: an entry applies to a GPU when the GPU's Name contains 'vendor' (and 'match' if set), case-insensitive, and 'side' is client/server/both. A version is flagged if it is in 'badVersions' (use ['*'] for any version of that adapter), inside 'range' [min,max] inclusive, or — for NVIDIA — matches 'nvidiaVersion'[..'nvidiaVersionMax']. NOTE ON VERSIONS: RDPeek reads the WMI DriverVersion (Win32_VideoController), which is the WDDM form. For NVIDIA that looks like 21.21.13.7849, NOT the GeForce '378.49' that forums cite — so NVIDIA entries use 'nvidiaVersion' (the branch version) and RDPeek decodes the WMI build to compare. Intel and AMD WMI versions (e.g. 31.0.101.5522, 31.0.21921.1000) are what those vendors ship, so use 'range'/'badVersions' for them. Entries below are curated from public bug reports; verify against your environment. Separately, any driver older than 'oldDriverMonths' gets a quiet, low-severity 'old driver' note.

entries.reason: GeForce 378.49 is a long-documented cause of a black screen over Remote Desktop (the desktop renders locally but RDP shows black).

NVIDIA GPU rendering over RDP on Windows Server 2025 has reports of pink/black UI artifacts and corruption. If you see them, try the newest supported branch, or disable 'Use the hardware default graphics adapter' for RDP.

Reproducible random black screen during mstsc sessions reported on Intel Core Ultra (Arc/Xe, WDDM 3.2) drivers in this range. Workarounds: update to the newest Core Ultra driver, or reduce GPU pressure; bumping TdrDelay has helped some.
The session host is on the Microsoft Basic Display Adapter (no vendor GPU driver) — GPU-accelerated RemoteFX/AVC encode is unavailable; expect software-only encoding.

Session is using the Microsoft Remote Display Adapter (indirect display) — normal for a headless/GPU-less host, but there is no hardware encode; if graphics feel slow, a real GPU with a current driver enables AVC/H.264 hardware encode.
